**Working Notes — Part 2/3 (Title I §229 PHS Act through Title V §528)**

**Office of the Secretary / General Departmental Management**
- $402,341,000 + $58,028,000 from PHS Act §241 for national health/human services research & evaluation.
- $28,000,000 for minority AIDS prevention/treatment.
- $40,000,000 for competitive grants exclusively implementing sexual risk avoidance education (voluntarily refraining from non-marital sexual activity); must use medically accurate peer-reviewed info, evidence-based approach, teach self-regulation, success sequencing, healthy relationships, goal setting, resisting coercion/violence/youth risk behaviors; no normalizing teen sexual activity; ≤10% for technical assistance/admin.
- Embryo adoption funds may provide medical/administrative services to individuals adopting embryos, consistent with 42 CFR 59.5(a)(4).
- $5,000,000 for prize competitions (Stevenson-Wydler Act §24, 15 U.S.C. 3719) on kidney disease prevention/diagnosis/treatment.

**Medicare Hearings and Appeals** — $196,000,000; $40,000,000 available through Sept 30, 2025; transferred from Federal Hospital Insurance & Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Funds.

**ONC for Health IT** — $56,238,000 from PHS Act §241 for interoperable health IT grants/contracts/cooperative agreements.

**Office of Inspector General (HHS)** — $80,000,000; includes protective services for Secretary and child support non-payment investigations (18 U.S.C. 228); activities under PHS Act §3022 (42 U.S.C. 300jj-52).

**Office for Civil Rights (HHS)** — $32,000,000.

**Retirement Pay & Medical Benefits (PHS Commissioned Officers)** — Such amounts as may be required; covers Retired Serviceman's Family Protection Plan, Survivor Benefit Plan, Dependents' Medical Care Act.

**Title I General Provisions (§§201–248)**
- §201: ≤$50,000 for official reception/representation (Secretary-approved).
- §202: Salary cap at Executive Level II for extramural grants; exception allows NIH to pay up to 100% at that rate.
- §203: No §241 PHS Act funds expended until Secretary reports planned uses to Appropriations Committees.
- §204: Notwithstanding §241(a) PHS Act, up to 2.5% of appropriated program funds available for evaluation.
- §205: ≤1% transfer between HHS appropriations; no appropriation increased >3%; no new programs; 15-day advance notice to Committees.
- §206: PHS Act §338E(c)(2) terminations may occur up to 60 days after FY2024 contract effective date under §338B, or anytime if unpaid.
- §207: Title X PHS Act applicants must certify encouraging family participation for minors seeking family planning and counseling on resisting sexual coercion.
- §208: Title X providers not exempt from State child abuse/molestation/rape/incest reporting laws.
- §209: No Medicare Advantage denial for entities refusing abortion provision/referral; Secretary adjusts capitation payments actuarially; entity must inform enrollees where to obtain Medicare-covered service info.
- §210: No funds to advocate/promote gun control.
- §211: ≤60 PHS employees assigned to child survival/AIDS programs via USAID, UNICEF, WHO.
- §212: HHS international health authority — Secretary may exercise State Dept. equivalent authority (State Dept. Basic Authorities Act §2(c)); fund facility acquisition/lease/renovation abroad; provide allowances/benefits similar to Foreign Service Act ch. 9 and 22 U.S.C. 4081–4086; locality-based comparability payments up to D.C. rate (5 U.S.C. §5304); leave per 5 U.S.C. ch. 63 subch. I or Foreign Service Act §903.
- §213: NIH Director + Office of AIDS Research Director may transfer ≤3% among institutes/centers for HIV research; 15-day notice.
- §214: HIV research amounts transferred to "Office of AIDS Research" account; Director transfers amounts for PHS Act §2353(d)(3).
- §215: NIH Director may use PHS Act §402(b)(12) funds for non-standard transactions; alternative peer review per Director's procedures in lieu of §§301(a)(3), 405(b)(1)(B), 405(b)(2), 406(a)(3)(A), 492, 494.
- §216: ≤$100,000,000 NIH funds for facility alteration/repair/improvement; ≤$5,000,000/project.
- §217: 1% of NRSA funds to HRSA Administrator for primary medical care research (entities under PHS Act §§736, 739, 747); 1% to AHRQ Director for health services research.
- §218: BARDA multi-year contracts (1–10 program years) for research services/security countermeasures (PHS Act §319F-2(c)(1)(B)); funds must be obligated for full period or first FY + termination costs; Secretary determines best interests; termination clause per 41 U.S.C. §3903(c); congressional notice per §3903(d).
